page.layout: Running head at top with page number at left; below it, the continuation of a verse poem in one full-width block; a printed ornament band (no text); a centred chapter heading "Caput quintum."; a centred summary line; then one column of verse stanzas numbered 1 to 4 in the left margin; a catchword at the right below the last line.

p.i: Jam te reviset Et tui miserata Cunctos labores finiet. Nec te subditam ad exteras Amplius procul urbes Migrare victor Coget acerbus. At tu patrum delicta cuncta mox lues, Factisque dignas impiis poenas Idume.
QVI cuncta celso despicis aethere Gentem benigno Lumine recrea Isacidarum, cerne quantis Illa probris agitata languet.
Miles superbo fortior agmine Irrupit urbes Barbarus, & domos: Nostrisque gens terris remota Vertit agros populata nostros.
Claris juventus orta parentibus Nunc luget omnis squallida: Perditi Conjunx mariti tam cruento Funera flet properata bello.

page.notes: Printed page 40 with running head LAMENTATIONES. The ornament band between the first poem and "Caput quintum." contains no text and is not transcribed. The faint text at the right edge is show-through from the other side of the leaf and is omitted. The long s is given as plain s throughout; i/j and u/v are normalised. "Isacidarum" was read from a slightly worn word (printed "Ifacidarum") and is the likely reading. The catchword "Ah," stands at the right below the last line. Verse numbers 1 to 4 stand in the left margin and are given as notes.
